verdict.label: not_replicated
verdict.rationale: Both claims concern metformin's within-group change from baseline in LDL-cholesterol, so the exposure, outcome and contrast type are comparable. Side A (PRIME-V RCT, Japanese type 2 diabetes patients on sitagliptin) reports that metformin 1000-1500 mg/day significantly reduced LDL-cholesterol over 24 weeks ('Metformin significantly reduced HbA1c and LDL-cholesterol levels and increased HOMA-beta'). Side B (RCT in overweight/obese PCOS women) reports no significant LDL-cholesterol change with metformin ('there were no significant changes in above parameters with metformin treatment') and draws the substantive conclusion that orlistat 'is superior to metformin in improvement of lipid metabolism', i.e., an explicit failure to show a metformin lipid effect. This abstract-level non-replication occurs against a specifically supported contextual difference: side A studied Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes on background sitagliptin for 24 weeks, while side B studied overweight/obese women with PCOS with unspecified metformin dose over 3-6 months, which may account for the divergent lipid results. Both extractions faithfully reflect their sources; no material extraction error was identified.

while there were no significant changes in above parameters with metformin treatment

orlistat is comparable with metformin in weight loss and improvement of insulin resistance and menstrual cycle, and is superior to metformin in improvement of lipid metabolism in overweight/obese PCOS patients.

diagnostics.notes: Side B's per-sentence wording is a significance statement ('no significant changes'), but its conclusion sentence provides an explicit substantive conclusion that metformin did not improve lipid metabolism, satisfying the not_replicated branch. The factor records the textually supported population/context difference (type 2 diabetes on sitagliptin vs PCOS; 24 weeks vs 3-6 months; metformin dose unreported in side B) rather than any extraction defect.
